extracted.intended_audience: parents and educators of girls and young women; general Victorian readers interested in education and domestic morality
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance (Victorian-era) on the proper education, character, artistic training, and social/domestic role of girls and women, and on how literature and nature should be used in that education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Woman's function as guide, not determiner
rubrics_metrics.description: The woman's office in marriage is a guiding, not a determining, function: she should guide her husband's choices and the household without usurping decisive authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish 'guiding' from 'determining'—the woman should direct by counsel and moral influence while leaving final determinations (especially public or combative duties) to the man. The guidance emphasizes complementary roles rather than superiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of a woman who rules well
rubrics_metrics.description: A woman who rightly fulfils her guiding role must be 'enduringly, incorruptibly good; instinctively, infallibly wise—wise, not for self-development, but for self-renunciation' and possess 'passionate gentleness' and an 'infinitely variable...modesty of service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These moral and temperamental qualities are framed as prerequisites for safe and beneficial female influence: incorruptible goodness, restrained wisdom directed to service, and adaptable modesty so she elevates those around her rather than domineers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical training and exercise to confirm health and beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure for girls such physical training and exercise as will confirm their health and perfect their beauty; beauty cannot be perfected without activity and delicate strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical freedom must be paired with 'freedom of heart'—exercise and bodily training are necessary but not sufficient; avoid excessive restraints that harden features and remove the brightness of innocence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty depends on happiness — 'vital feelings of delight'
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfect loveliness arises from 'vital feelings of delight'—a girl must be happy for beauty to be vital and attractive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot make a girl lovely if you do not make her happy; restraints or undue checks produce a hardness that destroys the charm of virtue. Encourage joyful, life-affirming experience as part of education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education content: know to feel and judge, not merely to accumulate facts
rubrics_metrics.description: A girl's knowledge should enable her to understand and aid men's work, but it should be given 'not as knowledge...for her an object to know; but only to feel, and to judge.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach habits of accurate thought, an understanding of natural laws, and some scientific attainment up to the 'threshold of the Valley of Humiliation'—enough to foster sympathy, judgement, and moral imagination rather than mere encyclopedic fact-holding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and literary imagination and sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Educate girls to 'enter with her whole personality into the history she reads; to picture the passages of it vitally' and to extend the limits of her sympathy to contemporary suffering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise imaginative apprehension and moral sympathy over abstract reasoning: train her to apprehend pathetic circumstances and dramatic relations, imagine the effects of suffering, and cultivate broad, active piety that embraces the desolate and oppressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid theology as a dangerous study for women
rubrics_metrics.description: Theology is identified as 'one dangerous science for women' that they should 'beware how they profanely touch' because it can produce pride, arrogance, and domestic discomfort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that plunging into theology without due humility may turn piety into conceit and domestic unrest. This is presented as an exception to the general parity of curriculum between sexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer depth over superficial or half-knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a wide difference between elementary knowledge and superficial knowledge—between a firm beginning and an infirm attempt at compassing; half-knowledge or mis-knowledge will only tease and harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure instruction is accurate and sufficiently deep for useful sympathy and contribution; avoid teaching in ways that leave the pupil half-informed or misinformed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different aims for male and female learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Men should learn thoroughly and progressively; women should know the same subjects 'only so far as may enable her to sympathise' in her husband's pleasures and be accomplished for daily use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum may be similar in content but must be differently directed: men's learning foundation and progression, women's learning practical, general, and tuned for social usefulness and sympathetic understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of reading: select books for their possession of good
rubrics_metrics.description: Books (novels, poetry, history) should be chosen 'not for their freedom from evil, but for their possession of good.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even powerful works may contain scattered evils; prefer authors with substance and goodness. Novels can be 'treatises on moral anatomy' but are often read without earnestness; beware over-wrought interest that makes ordinary life uninteresting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware over-wrought interest in novels and excitement
rubrics_metrics.description: The danger in novel reading is not necessarily moral badness but 'over-wrought interest' that renders ordinary life uninteresting and creates a morbid thirst for scenes one cannot act in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit novels whose excitement distorts temperament; prefer reading that enlarges sympathy and steadies character rather than foments morbid appetite for sensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic models should be 'truest, simplest, usefullest'
rubrics_metrics.description: In art and accomplishments, keep the finest models before her—'the truest, simplest, usefullest'—applied in music to mean notes that most faithfully express words, simplicity of means, and usefulness in making words memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach by the best models: truth and fidelity to meaning, economy and simplicity in expression, and usefulness—art that serves words and heart. In music: faithful expression, few significant notes, and functionally beautiful accompaniment to words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice in accomplishments must be accurate and thorough
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice in accomplishments should be accurate and thorough so as to enable her to 'understand more than she accomplishes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should aim at mastery sufficient for comprehension and sympathetic judgement, not mere superficial display; accuracy enables appreciation and useful application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education spirit: seriousness, courage, and truth preferred to ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring up girls as seriously as boys: appeal to 'the same grand instincts of virtue'; teach courage and truth rather than mere decorum or sideboard ornamentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of social systems that prioritize appearance; instill moral qualities (courage, sincerity) rather than excessive concern for manners and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and respect noble teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide girls with 'noble teachers' and show reverence to them as you would for men's tutors; the quality and social regard of teachers affects a girl's sense of her own intellect and importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't delegate girls' formation to poorly regarded instructors; consider the character of the master, accord them authority and respect, and do not treat them as domestic inferiors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure to wild and fair nature as essential educative influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The help of wild and fair nature is indispensable: children should have gardens, woods, and natural surroundings—'the fountains and forests' that nurture imagination and strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve natural playgrounds for children; value landscape, mountains, and sea as formative influences and moral schoolrooms. Criticises industrial/city encroachment that robs children of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home as sacred place of peace and woman's duty to secure it
rubrics_metrics.description: Home should be the place of Peace—a sacred, vestal temple watched by Household Gods; the woman’s function is to secure order, comfort, and loveliness so home shields from outer anxieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educative and social policies should aim to keep the anxieties of the outer world from penetrating the home; maintain domestic order and shelter so the household fulfils its moral role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer classical and old literature over modern magazines for girls
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep modern magazines and ephemeral novels away from girls; turn them to a good library of old and classical books where 'she will find what is good for her.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classical literature is less likely to excite frivolity; allow a girl's tastes to mature in a library of substantial works rather than the latest transient publications.
